description: This dataset label groups three distinct benign entities: seborrheic keratosis (a common, harmless warty skin growth associated with skin aging), solar lentigo (a flat pigmented patch on sun-exposed skin), and lichen-planus-like keratosis (an inflammatory, regressing phase of a seborrheic keratosis). Seborrheic keratosis is the primary and most thoroughly documented representative of this category.
taxonomy_note: BKL is a combined dataset category. Seborrheic keratosis, solar lentigo, and lichen-planus-like keratosis have different mechanisms and appearances; this entry is based primarily on seborrheic keratosis, the best-documented of the three, and should be treated as an approximation for the other two.
symptoms: Starts as a small, rough bump and slowly thickens, developing a warty, "stucco-like" surface
Color ranges from white to black, most commonly tan or brown
Size from a fraction of an inch up to more than an inch (roughly 1mm to several centimeters)
Occurs on the chest, back, stomach, scalp, face, neck, or other body areas, but not on palms or soles
Can be solitary or appear as multiple/grouped lesions
Usually painless; some itch or catch on clothing
warning_signs: Grows quickly, turns black, itches, or bleeds - possible signs of skin cancer rather than a typical seborrheic keratosis
Appears suddenly along with many other new skin growths - the sign of Leser-Trelat, which may denote an underlying internal malignancy, most often gastric adenocarcinoma
Looks dry, flat, rough, and scaly - could instead be an actinic keratosis, which can progress toward skin cancer
Becomes easily irritated, for example from shaving or clothing
recommendation: Most seborrheic keratoses are harmless and do not require treatment; do not attempt to remove one at home due to infection risk. See a dermatologist if any of the warning signs above are present, since they may indicate a different, non-benign condition rather than the seborrheic keratosis itself becoming malignant.
